teachingPoints.objective: Retain all three go/come/be senses with honorific marking.

teachingPoints.objective: Honor the president's arrival while also using a polite ending.

teachingPoints.objective: Invite the guest to eat with an honorific te-form request, not the speaker-humble verb.

teachingPoints.objective: Read the Japanese label for humble language.
Include the speaker's represented in-group in humble perspective without lowering a client.
teachingPoints.prompt: Whose action is normally presented modestly with humble language?
teachingPoints.answer: The speaker's own action or an action of someone represented as part of the speaker's group.

teachingPoints.objective: Map the raise-others/lower-self mnemonic precisely to sonkeigo and kenjougo.
teachingPoints.prompt: Map the cue raise others, lower self to the two respectful language categories.
teachingPoints.answer: Raise others maps to 尊敬語 (そんけいご); lower self or one's group maps to 謙譲語 (けんじょうご).

Read the full humble viewing compound rather than saving a paradigm ending.

teachingPoints.objective: Introduce one's name humbly rather than honorifically elevating oneself.
teachingPoints.prompt: 田中と___。 (My name is Tanaka; humble polite form.)

teachingPoints.objective: Conjugate the suru part of humble viewing in a polite past email report.
teachingPoints.prompt: メールを___。 (I read your email; humble polite past.)

teachingPoints.objective: Complete the established formal greeting without generalizing gozaimasu to every verb.
teachingPoints.prompt: おはよう___。

teachingPoints.objective: Keep de in the formal service copular construction.
teachingPoints.prompt: お手洗いはあちら___。 (Use the formal service equivalent of です.)

teachingPoints.objective: Reject an exclusive five-rung model by distinguishing respectful reference from listener politeness.
teachingPoints.prompt: Does using いらっしゃいます mean choosing honorific language instead of polite language?
teachingPoints.answer: No. The verb honors the person described, and its ます ending also makes the sentence polite toward the listener.

teachingPoints.objective: Avoid automatically copying a senior's casual register across an asymmetric relationship.
teachingPoints.prompt: Should you automatically copy a senior's casual endings when speaking back to them?
teachingPoints.answer: No. Consider the relationship, setting, and whether a shared move to casual speech is appropriate.
